BioNova Therapeutics - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the BioNova Therapeutics Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone and wait for further instructions. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss BioNova Therapeutics' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer; Lisa Wong, Head of Commercial; and Tom Reilly, Head of Manufacturing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO of BioNova Therapeutics.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. BioNova Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the second quarter, driven by robust product sales growth, margin expansion from manufacturing efficiencies, and continued pipeline advancement. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives. We saw impressive gross margin trends, with GAAP gross margins expanding to 82.3%, fueled by favorable product mix and manufacturing gains. Our R&D investments prioritized high-potential assets in oncology and rare diseases, while operating expenses reflected disciplined growth. New product launches like Novaxa drove market share gains, our key franchises delivered solid volume and pricing dynamics, overall results beat expectations, and business development deals added substantial value. We are particularly excited about NovaTrastuzumab and its potential to transform HER2-positive cancer treatment with premium pricing and strong uptake.

Now, I will turn the call over to Mike Chen, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Mike Chen, CFO:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a solid second quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $1.34 billion, an increase of 18% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by strong performance across our oncology and immunology franchises, with notable contributions from new launches and volume growth in key markets.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $265 million, or $1.52 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $320 million, or $1.85 per share.

Our operating expenses were $452 million, reflecting a 12% year-over-year increase as we ramped investments in late-stage trials and commercial efforts. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to support our pipeline, with Q2 spend at $428 million. Our cash position remains strong at $3.2 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to revenue of $5.2 to $5.4 billion, EPS of $7.40 to $7.70, and R&D expenses of $1.7 to $1.8 billion.

Let me dive deeper into some key areas. Starting with gross margin trends and manufacturing efficiency, which remain a cornerstone of our financial performance. Our GAAP gross margin expanded to 82.3% in Q2, up 450 basis points year-over-year from 77.8% and 120 basis points sequentially from Q1's 81.1%. On a non-GAAP basis, excluding one-time charges from a legacy small-molecule API supply disruption, it reached 83.5%—our strongest quarterly result since the launch of NovaTrastuzumab in 2021. This beat our guidance midpoint and outperformed peers like Regeneron at 81% and Amgen at 79%.

Key drivers included product mix adding 250 basis points, with NovaTrastuzumab now at 42% of revenue—up from 35% YoY—on 28% volume growth outpacing the U.S. ADC market. NovaLiraglutide gained share in obesity, contributing high margins over 85%. Pricing added 100 basis points from U.S. adjustments on NovaTrastuzumab, offset by European tenders. Biosimilars like NovaHumira added 150 basis points with 15% U.S. market share.

Manufacturing efficiency drove 300 basis points of improvement, with COGS per unit down 18% to $42,000 for biologics. Process intensification at Singapore boosted titers 105% to 8.2 g/L, cutting cycle times 40% using PAT and Raman spectroscopy—reducing failures to under 0.5%. Capacity utilization hit 92% across Devens, Limerick, Singapore, and Suzhou sites. Supply chain resilience derisked 85% of inputs, capping inflation at 4% via multi-sourcing with Lonza and WuXi, plus AI predictive maintenance saving $25 million annually.

We're targeting 85-87% margins by 2026, investing $300 million in gene therapy vectors and digital twins. Q3 guidance is 82-83%, full-year 81.5-82.5%.

Turning to R&D expense and pipeline investment priorities, Q2 R&D was $428 million, up 18% YoY, or 32% of revenue—tracking to $1.7-1.8 billion full-year. Allocation: 45% late-stage, 30% early-stage, 15% CMC, 10% platforms. Oncology 42%, immunology 28%, rare diseases 18%, neuroscience 12%. Our 28-asset pipeline includes NB-ADC-301 in Phase III oncology ($185 million invested), NB-IL23i oral IL-23 inhibitor in Phase IIb, and NB-GT-101 gene therapy for Pompe under RMAT.

R&D intensity at 29% is competitive, uplifted by AI nominating 12 targets. Externalization covers 25% via BeiGene on NB-BiTE-045. Regionally, 55% U.S., 25% Europe with €15 million funding, 20% Asia. Q3 at $440-460 million including a PI3Kδ in-license.

On operating expense analysis, total OpEx was $452 million, 28% of TTM revenue—below peer medians. R&D at $308 million (68%), up 18% on Phase 3 for BNT-401 ($45 million trials, $22 million CMC with Lonza, $15 million Exscientia milestones). Savings of $18 million via outsourcing and AI. SG&A $144 million flat YoY: sales/marketing $68 million for NovaShield launch (12% share), G&A $76 million with Dublin efficiencies.

We're targeting 500 bps expansion by 2026 via AI ($50 million savings) and outsourcing.

Product revenue by key franchises totaled $2.48 billion, up 18% reported, 21% CER. Oncology $1.12 billion (+22%), NovaCheck $892 million (16% volume, ASP $148,000); BioTarget-301 $228 million. Immunology $685 million (+15%), NovaMab-R $610 million (13% volume). Rare Diseases $420 million (+28%), GeneFix-H volumes doubled. Metabolic $235 million (+85%), NovaGLP-2 ramped. U.S. 69%, Q3 guide $2.55-2.65 billion.

Overall performance highlights: total revenue $1.34 billion (28% YoY), NovaCure $850 million (66%), GeneXpert $220 million. Adjusted EPS $1.85 beating estimates. Margins 87%, R&D $420 million supporting 12 readouts. U.S. 72%, Europe 18%, Asia 10%. Raised FY guidance. Fortress balance sheet.

Business development included $450 million upfront from CKD for NB-ADC-301 in Asia ($2.1 billion milestones), $250 million out-license NB-GT-102, $1.2 billion SynthoGenix acquisition (SGX-777 KRAS degrader), Merck co-dev for NB-IO-520 ($600 million upfront). $1.8 billion funding, $20 billion funnel.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Mike. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, NB-ADC-301 is fully enrolled in Phase III for metastatic breast cancer, with data Q4 2025; NB-IL23i accelerated enrollment 22% in Phase IIb psoriasis; NB-GT-101 dosed first Pompe patient under RMAT. BNT-401 at 85% enrollment. We expect three BLA filings by year-end and four potential approvals by 2025, including CAR-T combos.

Next, Dr. Raj Patel will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Elena. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Advancements include AI/ML for 15% success uplift, PROTAC library, CRISPR CAR-NK cells 3x more potent than Yescarta, and mRNA platforms. We've pruned low-confidence assets, redirecting to degraders and bispecifics like NB-IO-520 with 68% regression.

Now I'll turn the call over to Lisa Wong, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Lisa Wong, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Raj. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with $2.48 billion in product revenue. Novaxa generated $285 million, 7.2% U.S. share in HER2 breast cancer, 12% in gastric—92% U.S., early Europe €22 million. NovaTrastuzumab 42% revenue, NovaLiraglutide 18%. NovaShield 12% RSV share, NovaCure 18% NSCLC. Marketing via DTC, KOLs, patient platforms enrolled 4,200 for Novaxa, driving 28% prescription growth.

Finally, Tom Reilly will discuss our manufacturing operations.

Tom Reilly, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Lisa. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. Utilization 92% across four sites: continuous perfusion in Singapore (titers 8.2 g/L), Suzhou ramp to 50%, single-use bioreactors cutting costs 22%. AI maintenance cut downtime 35%, dual-sourcing 85% inputs. Scaled Novaxa to 50,000 vials/month, GeneFix-H yields +40%, metabolic fill-finish optimized. Focused on viral vectors, modular cleanrooms, sustainable chemistry for 30% Scope 3 cuts.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Alex.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Tom. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, to ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee, Morgan Stanley:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On gross margins, the 83.5% non-GAAP beat was impressive—can you elaborate on the manufacturing drivers and sustainability into 2026?

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thanks, David. Mike, do you want to take that?

Mike Chen, CFO:
Sure, Alex. As detailed, product mix from NovaTrastuzumab and NovaLiraglutide added 250 bps, but manufacturing was key with 300 bps from Singapore perfusion (105% titer uplift, 40% cycle cut), 92% utilization, and supply resilience capping inflation at 4%. $300 million capex targets 85-87% by 2026 via vectors and digital twins. Q3 82-83% despite one-offs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen, JPMorgan:
Great, thanks. On R&D at $428 million, how are you prioritizing oncology versus rare diseases, and any updates on regional spend?

Mike Chen, CFO:
Thanks, Emily. Oncology 42% with $185 million on NB-ADC-301 Phase III, immunology 28% on NB-IL23i (22% enrollment acceleration), rare diseases 18% highest ROI with $120 million on NB-GT-101 Pompe RMAT. 55% U.S., 25% Europe (€15M funding), 20% Asia leveraging faster timelines. AI uplifts success 15%, external 25% non-dilutive.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Gupta with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Raj Gupta, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks. For clinical programs, thoughts on BNT-401 Phase 3 and combo data risks?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer:
Hi Raj. BNT-401 PD-1/VEGF bispecific 85% enrolled across 120 sites, topline Q4 2024 for BLA H1 2025. Like Keytruda follow-ons, adaptive designs and Lonza CMC derisk it. Combos with NB-402 show 25% PFS uplift in NOVELATE.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim, Bank of America:
Thanks. Lisa, on Novaxa launch, share trajectory to 9-10% in Q3 and payer dynamics?

Lisa Wong, Head of Commercial:
Thanks, Sarah. Q2 7.2% U.S. HER2 share, 12% gastric—$285M sales, 18% gross-to-net on 85% Tier 1 coverage. ASCO neuropathy data drove 65% high-decile scripts. Q3 $350-380M, 9-10% as community oncology hits 40%, VBAs de-risk rebates.

Operator:
Our next question is a follow-up from David Lee with Morgan Stanley.

David Lee, Morgan Stanley:
Quick one on BD—details on the Merck PD-1 x LAG-3 deal and M&A pipeline?

Mike Chen, CFO:
David, Merck co-dev NB-IO-520: $600M upfront, $3.2B milestones, 50/50 split—68% regression preclinical. CKD $450M for NB-ADC-301 Asia, SynthoGenix $1.2B KRAS PROTAC. Funnel $20B, prioritizing GLP-1 and CAR-T.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thanks, everyone.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the BioNova Therapeutics Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
